newsitem.title: UK: Gold locked above $346, palladium slips further.
newsitem.headline: Gold locked above $346, palladium slips further.

text.p: The price of gold was locked in a tight band above $346 on Monday with underlying physical offtake providing a cushion against further drops, dealers said.

Bullion fixed barely changed on Tuesday afternoon at $346.75 versus $346.65 in the morning and well above the nadir of $345.30 to which it was slashed by funds in New York on Friday after disappointing U.S. inflation data.
"On the fall on Friday there was good fund selling and there was very good physical offtake. Today at the level where we have settled we haven't seen anything at all," said one dealer.
But gold could hang around $346-$347 this week or it could have another bash on the upside and try to take $350 out, he said.
Despite gold's downside risk, most market analysts see the $345-$346 area as a sponge, ready to absorb a flare up in sales.
But upside prospects are also seen limited, mainly because of expected interest rate hikes needed to cool the U.S. economy. Higher rates make gold look less attractive as an investment.

"...more and more dealers (are) expecting rallies to above $355 to be drowned in an avalanche of forward selling by producers and dealers alike," said Merrill Lynch in a monthly report. That selling deluge could send prices down to $340.
Fresh clues on interest rates will be provided by U.S. consumer prices and industrial production data this week.
Some analysts said the market was prone to a breach of $345.
"If we cannot hold $345.20, I expect stop loss orders and this could take the market to $341 and maybe test the lows of the year," said a senior dealer in continental Europe.
Palladium lost its shine, trading nervously at around $152.00 after a dip to $151.10. It came down since last week's spike to $160 after news Russian supplies to Japan could resume in May.
"If a story saying the opposite thing could quite reasonably come out the market will be back in the 160," said a dealer.
But despite easier prices, palladium forwards were tight with one month lease rates quoted at 10 percent.
"It is very expensive to run short positions," he said.
Russian exports have been delayed by four months now due to what is perceived as bureaucratic and political snags.

But Merill Lynch said in their report: "Palladium prices are nowhere near as high as one would expect given that the world's largest supplier has not sold an ounce to Japan...since December. This suggest to us that actual supplies of palladium are nowhere near as short as some bulls think."
Silver was six cents down on the day at $4.72/$4.74 and just off from Friday's lows, but analysts said a double bottom formation on charts at $4.70 could act as a magnet.
